gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-sharada: Clean and techy, Quantum spaces its letters loosely and keeps its mouths open. Noto Sans Sharada sits underneath it as a bulky, professional sans, and the two make the page feel sturdy.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Quantum draws its letters like bent wire, tubular and light, with generous gaps between them. Noto Sans Siddham answers with a big central band of lowercase, friendly and solid.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Noto Sans Sinhala lays down a thick, dark stripe of lowercase. Quantum above it is a single-depth engraver's cut with loose spacing, so the heading stays light while the text carries the weight.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Contemporary and professional in feel, Noto Sans Soyombo has a sizable x-height and curves that stay wide open, set under Quantum's pressure-free strokes. Lines move along smoothly.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-sundanes: Quantum looks like a bent paperclip, its line never swelling or thinning, with loose spacing and short ascenders. It handles the display work, while Noto Sans Sundanese quietly carries the text.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Noto Sans Sunuwar reads friendly and clean, with curves that leave daylight and short ascender stems on tall bodies. Quantum is the better headline voice, tracing a rolling-ball pen's single-width trail, while Noto Sans Sunuwar is the one for running text.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-syloti-n: Clean and crisp, Quantum draws its g in one unchanging line. Noto Sans Syloti Nagri follows with short ascenders, a tall x-height and an open lower bowl on the a, which makes long reading feel easy.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Noto Sans Syriac reads approachable and modern, its tall bowls like blown glass bulbs and its s turns wide and easy. And under Quantum's thread of ink, a long stretch of text feels relaxed and smooth.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-syriac-e: Quantum's stems and curves look cut from a single gauge of tubing, loosely spaced and open-mouthed. Noto Sans Syriac Eastern keeps tall lowercase against small caps, and its curve endings stay apart over a long stretch.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-syriac-w: Loose, open and techy. Noto Sans Syriac Western packs its small letters as thick as bundled cable, with terminals held far from the stroke, so a long passage reads modern and clean.
